questions.q: Why has 'is this data encrypted at rest' stopped being the interesting governance question in Azure and AWS?
options: Because encryption at rest is now optional and rarely used
Because only on-premises systems still require manual encryption configuration
Because neither cloud supports encryption at rest anymore
Because encryption at rest is now the default across major storage services in both clouds — the real question is who controls the key
questions.explain: Both clouds encrypt data at rest by default now, which shifts the meaningful governance decision onto key ownership and control, not whether encryption happens at all.

questions.q: In Azure Key Vault, what has to happen before a secret's plaintext value becomes visible?
options: The secret must first be deleted and recreated
Nothing — the value is always visible by default when viewing the secret
An explicit, separate, logged action — selecting Show Secret Value
Only the vault owner's password, entered once per session
questions.explain: Metadata is visible by default, but the value itself requires an explicit Show Secret Value action, which is a separate, auditable event.

questions.q: What does the 'Origin' field on an AWS KMS key's Cryptographic configuration tab indicate?
options: The IAM user who created the key
Where the key material came from — AWS KMS-generated, imported, or backed by AWS CloudHSM
Whether the key is symmetric or asymmetric
Which AWS Region the key was created in
questions.explain: Origin specifically describes the source of the key material (AWS KMS, imported/external, or CloudHSM-backed), distinct from Key Type, Key Spec, and Key Usage.

questions.q: What is the practical consequence of revoking a customer-managed key that's actively encrypting live data?
options: Nothing happens until the next scheduled key rotation
The data automatically re-encrypts itself under a platform-managed key
Every object encrypted under that key becomes unreadable immediately, everywhere
Only new writes are affected; existing encrypted data remains readable
questions.explain: Revocation is immediate and total — it's exactly why regulated workloads often require customer-managed keys specifically, for that instant revocation guarantee.

questions.q: Which key tier can an organization rotate on its own schedule, restrict access to with its own policy, and revoke entirely?
options: Customer-managed keys
None — all key tiers are controlled exclusively by the cloud provider
AWS managed keys / Microsoft-managed keys only
AWS owned keys / Azure platform-managed keys
questions.explain: Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are the tier the account itself fully controls — rotation, access policy, and revocation are all in the customer's hands.
